families.source_family: Standard setup, beginner alternatives, solo and physical/spatial preparation

primary_source_refs.locator: CORE first-time players and standard setup

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: For two Spirits, how are the Fear pool/deck and Invader deck prepared, what initial Blight pool is used with and without a Blight Card, and what final Invader action completes setup?
actual_required_facts: Two Spirits use 8 Fear markers.
Shuffle and use 9 Fear cards in three groups of 3 separated by Terror II/III.
Prepare 3 random Stage I above 4 Stage II above 5 Stage III, removing one unseen card of each stage.
Initial Healthy pool is 5; initial no-card pool is 11, including exactly one setup bonus.
Finish setup with a normal Explore and leave that card face-up in Build.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: Where does setup Blight come from versus Blight added during play? When a Healthy card empties how is its new pool obtained, does the setup +1 repeat, and can removing Blight make it Healthy again?
actual_required_facts: Setup island Blight comes from the box; play Blight comes from the card/board pool.
On Healthy pool exhaustion flip and follow the reverse instructions, adding its printed new per-player pool from the box.
The setup +1 does not repeat on a flip.
Removing Blight never flips a Blighted card back to Healthy.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: How is a Spirit’s starting hand obtained, where is its setup Presence placed, what if multiple legal setup choices or two placement instructions name the same land, and is its later play confined to that board?
actual_required_facts: Start with the Spirit's four Unique cards in hand.
Each Spirit starts on a different board and follows its back-panel setup.
Choose freely among equally legal setup choices.
Separate placement instructions may name the same land.
After setup Presence and Powers may operate on other boards.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: How does one-Spirit solo change Another Spirit targeting and conditional other-Spirit bonuses? Does one human playing two Spirits get that same self-targeting exception or use one-person setup scaling?
actual_required_facts: A one-Spirit solo game may target itself with Another Spirit.
Bonuses conditioned on actually targeting a different Spirit do not activate.
One person playing two Spirits fills two player roles and scales setup by two.
It does not get the single-Spirit self-target exception.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: Do low-complexity Spirits always have to use Power Progression? If used, how are gains and Major Forgetting handled, and how does the introductory no-Blight-Card game end from Blight?
actual_required_facts: Power Progression is an optional teaching aid, not compulsory for low-complexity Spirits.
When used, take the next listed card rather than draw 4/keep 1.
Gaining a Major still requires Forgetting.
In the no-card introductory game, emptying the board Blight pool loses without a flip.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: In standard setup using a Blight Card, how is the card chosen, which side starts face-up, and may players inspect its reverse before choosing or starting?
actual_required_facts: Choose a random Blight Card.
Start Healthy Island face-up.
Do not inspect its reverse before choosing/starting.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: For a standard game, how many balanced Island Boards are used and chosen, how are their initial Invaders, Dahan and Blight placed, and how are the Minor/Major decks and shared piece supplies prepared?
actual_required_facts: Randomly choose one balanced Island Board per Spirit and assemble the island.
Populate all lands using printed Invader, Dahan and Blight setup icons.
Take setup island Blight from the box rather than the pool.
Shuffle Minor and Major decks separately and provide separate shared discard spaces.
Prepare accessible shared supplies of Energy, Invaders and Dahan.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: After a Spirit has followed its back-panel island setup, where are its remaining Presence disks put? Are the leftmost solid-circle Energy and Card Plays numbers covered?
actual_required_facts: After island setup, put remaining Presence on the dashed circles of the Spirit panel's Presence tracks.
Leave the leftmost solid-circle Energy and Card Plays numbers uncovered.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: When using a beginner Spirit’s Power Progression, what must be done during setup with the Minor and Major cards listed on that Progression? Should they stay in the shared shuffled decks to be drawn normally by other gains?
actual_required_facts: During Power Progression setup, set aside all listed Minor and Major Power Cards.
Those reserved cards do not remain in the shared shuffled decks for ordinary draws.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: Do the normal cascade and one-Presence-per-Spirit destruction rules apply to Blight placed during setup, or only to Blight added after setup?
actual_required_facts: Setup Blight does not trigger the normal cascade rule.
Setup Blight does not destroy Presence; those normal adverse addition consequences apply after setup.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: In the first ordinary turn after standard setup, the Ravage Action Space has no Invader Card. Do Invaders Ravage anyway or draw a card for Ravage, or is that action omitted? What is the general rule for an empty Invader Action Space?
actual_required_facts: No Invader action is taken for a space with no Invader Card.
The first ordinary empty Ravage space therefore causes no Ravage: do not draw a Ravage card or invent a terrain for it.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: In a standard two-Spirit game with balanced Island Boards, must the boards use only the illustrated bottom-to-bottom layout, or may players join them in another arrangement that fits?
actual_required_facts: Any fitting arrangement of the two balanced boards is legal; the illustrated bottom-to-bottom orientation is not required.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: A copy of the core game contains 14 Presence disks of one color. Should all 14 be used for that Spirit's setup and later Presence availability, or is one a spare?
actual_required_facts: Use 13 Presence of that color; the extra disk is a spare and is not available for setup or later gameplay.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: In standard one-Spirit solo, are any of the eight original-core Spirits prohibited because their special restrictions appear to require teammates, including Ocean's Hungry Grasp or Bringer of Dreams and Nightmares?
actual_required_facts: None are prohibited: all eight original-core Spirits are permitted in solo, including the named Ocean and Bringer.

families.source_based_comparison: Checked distinct starting boards, back-panel placement, reserved Progression cards, random separate decks, initial Explore and extra setup Blight. Q22 actually requires different starting boards; Q17 actually requires reshuffling when needed. No false gap based on omitted shorthand. Optional easier-game bonus Growth/omitted Explore is difficulty adjustment outside assigned scope.

families.source_family: Spirit Phase, Growth, resources, Reclaim and card zones

primary_source_refs.locator: CORE Spirit Phase and phase ordering

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: A Spirit chooses Growth with two Add Presence actions. May the second placement use the first as its range origin? Which Presence-track disks may be taken, and how do uncovered Energy/Card Plays numbers combine?
actual_required_facts: Resolve the two placement actions in chosen order; the first new Presence may originate the second.
Take the leftmost remaining disk of either selected track for each placement.
Only the highest uncovered Energy and Card Plays numbers apply; do not add numbers.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: A Spirit has no Presence on its tracks but has Presence on the island and some destroyed disks. How can an Add Presence instruction be resolved, where is range measured, and can destroyed disks be used?
actual_required_facts: With tracks empty, reposition one of that Spirit's island Presence.
Measure the legal destination from existing island Presence, including the disk about to be repositioned, before picking a disk up.
Any of its island disks may supply the placement.
Destroyed disks cannot supply ordinary Add Presence without explicit permission.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: When are Fast and Slow Power Cards paid for and their Elements gained? Can promised Fast-phase Energy pay for the Spirit-phase cards, and do unspent Energy or unused Card Plays carry over?
actual_required_facts: Play and pay for both Fast and Slow cards during Spirit Phase.
Their Elements become available immediately on play/payment.
Fast-phase Energy arrives too late to pay these normal Spirit-phase costs.
Energy carries over; unused Card Plays do not.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: May a Fast Power wait until Slow, may Powers interrupt each other, and when must a Slow Power’s target be selected?
actual_required_facts: Fast Powers must resolve in Fast or be foregone; they cannot wait until Slow.
Finish one Power before another; Powers cannot interrupt one another.
Choose a Slow Power's target when it is used in Slow, using the then-current position and restrictions.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: A Growth option includes an impossible instruction and an explicit cost. Can it be selected, can possible instructions be skipped, and may one Spirit wait for another’s Growth result before choosing?
actual_required_facts: An impossible non-cost Growth instruction does not prevent selecting that option.
Do all possible instructions; do not voluntarily skip mandatory possible parts.
An explicit Growth cost must be paid fully.
A Spirit may wait for another's Growth result.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: What cards does ordinary Reclaim return, and when and how often can a newly uncovered Reclaim One space be used?
actual_required_facts: Ordinary Reclaim returns all personal-discard cards to hand, not in-play or forgotten cards.
Reclaim One returns one personal-discard card once per Spirit Phase at any time during that phase.
It is available the turn uncovered.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: When a track Element is revealed after Growth, when does it become usable? When may an Any track Element be chosen and changed, and what if an in-play card is Forgotten?
actual_required_facts: A revealed track Element is usable immediately and remains available while uncovered.
Choose a passive Any at any time during the turn; once chosen it is fixed until next turn.
Forgetting an in-play card removes that card's Elements immediately.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: What is the difference between a Growth Move Presence arrow and Add Presence using an island disk? Can the latter pick up a disk outside the shown Range of the destination?
actual_required_facts: Growth Move Presence measures up to the indicated distance from that disk's current land.
Add Presence using an island disk first selects a destination measured from existing Presence.
It may then take an island disk from anywhere, even outside the shown destination Range.
Repositioning under Add is adding rather than a Move instruction.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: May a newly gained Growth Power be played in the same Spirit Phase? Does a Power gained in Fast automatically enter play or resolve immediately, and is there a hand-size or hand-secrecy limit?
actual_required_facts: A Growth-gained card may be played later in the same Spirit Phase.
A Fast-gained card does not automatically enter play.
Gaining that card in Fast does not automatically resolve its effects immediately.
There is no hand-size limit and cards may be shown to others.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: When players disagree about a Power’s choices, a Blight cascade destination, or a decision outside any land, who ultimately decides?
actual_required_facts: The Power user decides Power choices.
For other decisions seek consensus.
Without consensus, a decision within/about a land belongs to the Spirit starting on that board.
A non-land decision falls to the owner/organizer.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: Can a Spirit give its unused Energy or Card Plays to another Spirit, or save unused Card Plays for the next turn? How does this differ from an explicit Power that grants another Spirit Energy or an extra play?
actual_required_facts: There is no ordinary transfer of individual Energy or Card Plays.
Unused Card Plays cannot be saved for the next turn.
Explicit Powers granting Energy or extra plays follow their instructions and can give those benefits.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: A Spirit has several separate Growth options and no instruction allowing more than one choice. During one Spirit Phase, may it combine the Energy action from one option with the Add Presence action from a different option, or must it choose a single entire option?
actual_required_facts: Without permission for more, choose one whole Growth option.
Do not combine actions from different options or choose multiple options.
Perform all possible instructions in the selected option.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: What is the required order of an individual Spirit's Growth, normal track Energy gain, and actual playing/paying for Power Cards? May the Spirit take its normal Energy income before finishing Growth or actually play/pay before Growth? If Growth uncovers a higher Energy number, is that number used for normal income in this same Spirit Phase?
actual_required_facts: Complete Growth, then gain normal track Energy, then actually play/pay Power Cards.
Normal income may not be taken before finishing Growth.
Actual normal card play/payment may not precede Growth.
The immediately following normal income step uses the newly uncovered highest number in this same Spirit Phase.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: A Spirit still has Presence disks on its Presence tracks. When resolving an ordinary Add Presence instruction, may it choose to reposition one of its Presence already on the island instead of taking a track disk, or is repositioning permitted only after its tracks are empty?
actual_required_facts: Yes: ordinary Add Presence may use an own island disk instead of a track disk even before tracks are empty.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: List the five phases of an ordinary turn in order. If one Spirit has finished playing and paying while another is still choosing Growth, may the first begin resolving a Fast Power? Within the Fast Power Phase, must Powers follow player order, or may players choose their sequence?
actual_required_facts: The ordinary five-phase order is Spirit Phase, Fast Power Phase, Invader Phase, Slow Power Phase, then Time Passes.
No Spirit may begin resolving Fast Powers until all Spirits have completed the Spirit Phase.
Within the Fast Power Phase players may choose the sequence of Powers; no fixed player order is required.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: When Green adds Presence via Growth, may it use destroyed disks while tracks still contain Presence? What is the price while Healthy versus Blighted? Does this special rule also let an ordinary Power Add Presence use destroyed disks?
actual_required_facts: Destroyed Presence may optionally supply Green’s Growth placements before tracks are empty.
This use is free while Healthy and costs 1 Energy per destroyed Presence added while Blighted.
Steady Regeneration applies to Growth, so an ordinary Power placement needs its own destroyed-Presence permission.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: Ocean has previously Drowned Invaders stored on its panel. Between actions in a later Spirit Phase, may it exchange them for Energy to help pay for cards that turn, or must it wait for another Drowning or the Gain Energy step?
actual_required_facts: Ocean may exchange stored Drowned Invaders at the stated between-actions time in the later Spirit Phase; it need not wait for another Drowning or the normal Gain Energy step.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: Ocean chooses its Growth option with two “Add a Presence in any Ocean” instructions. May one disk be placed in the Ocean of a different island board where Ocean currently has no Presence, without measuring a numeric Range from its existing Presence?
actual_required_facts: The explicit any-Ocean Growth instruction may place in another board’s Ocean without preexisting Presence there or a numeric Range origin.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: Green chooses its Reclaim-and-gain-Power Growth group. Does it also perform the separate ALWAYS Add Presence to Jungle/Wetland, or must it choose between that addition and Reclaim?
actual_required_facts: Green performs the separate ALWAYS placement in addition to the selected Reclaim-and-gain-Power Growth group.

families.source_based_comparison: Compared per-Spirit Grow/Gain/Play order with cross-Spirit simultaneity, whole-option selection, chaining/repositioning, actual track benefits, passive Any/ReclaimOne and new Green/Ocean permissions. Do not credit unverified full-Growth-option cost simply because Green has an optional per-disk regeneration price.

families.source_family: Gaining, Forgetting, gifts and additional play/Repeat timing

primary_source_refs.locator: Additional plays and independent Forget costs

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: Explain gaining a new Minor or Major Power, including how many are drawn, where kept/unkept cards go, Major Forgetting options and the consequences of Forgetting a card already in play.
actual_required_facts: Choose Minor or Major and draw 4, reshuffling that deck's discard if needed.
Keep one in hand and put unkept cards in their deck's shared discard.
Gaining a Major requires Forgetting one owned card, including hand/discard/in-play/new Major options.
Forgotten Minor/Major goes to its deck discard; Unique goes under its panel.
Forgetting an in-play card removes its Elements and any unused use immediately.
Already resolved effects persist for their normal duration.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: An effect explicitly allows playing a card in Fast after the Spirit used all normal Card Plays. Is this legal and when are its Elements/effects available?
actual_required_facts: An explicit effect-granted Fast-phase play is additional to ordinary Card Plays and is legal after they are exhausted.
Gain its Elements immediately when played.
Resolve it at its Speed in the proper phase outside another action unless explicitly told otherwise.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: If Entwined Power gifts a Major Power, must the recipient Forget? If a Spirit instead gains two Majors, can a single Forget cover both? Is an ordinary forgotten Unique reclaimable?
actual_required_facts: Entwined gifting/transferring a Major is not Gain and requires no Forget.
Two Major gains require two separate Forgets; one card cannot pay both.
A normally Forgotten Unique is under the panel and not ordinarily reclaimable.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: When a Fast Gift of Strength or Powerstorm grants a Repeat, must the card be chosen immediately? Can the chosen card be Slow, can it be an innate, and do you gain its printed Elements again?
actual_required_facts: Choose a card for the granted Repeat when actually using the option, not necessarily when granted.
A Slow card can be chosen and repeated in Slow.
Gift of Strength/Powerstorm say Power Card and cannot repeat an Innate.
Repeating does not grant printed card Elements again.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: What happens when Powerstorm itself is Repeated, and can its threshold spend all three Repeat permissions on the same Power Card?
actual_required_facts: Ignore Repeat instructions when repeating Powerstorm; it grants no further Repeat permissions.
Its non-Repeat Energy gain still resolves.
Its threshold permits up to three different cards, not three repetitions of the same card.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: In solo, what does Entwined Power grant from its normal gain wording and its Energy threshold? Can gifting another Spirit a Unique with a defined special effect such as Drown still use that definition?
actual_required_facts: In solo Entwined's normal gain wording can give two Power Cards.
Its threshold can give 6 Energy.
A gifted card can still use a defined effect such as Drown.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: In Call on Midnight’s Dreams, which card is this Power for its Forget conditional? Must Bringer Forget a second card beyond the ordinary Major gain requirement to activate it, and can the forgotten original later be Repeated with Powerstorm?
actual_required_facts: This Power means Call on Midnight's Dreams itself.
Forgetting it for the ordinary Major gain requirement also satisfies its conditional; no second Forget is required.
Once Forgotten it leaves play and cannot later be Repeated with Powerstorm's ordinary once-this-turn permission.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: A Spirit plays two Power Cards and later Repeats one. For an effect counting Power Cards played, such as Boon of Vigor, is the count two or three? Does the Repeat consume another ordinary Card Play, and does it nevertheless count as a new Power use?
actual_required_facts: Count two cards played, not three; Repeat does not play another card.
Repeat consumes no extra ordinary Card Play.
It nevertheless counts as a new Power use.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: A Spirit has met an unused Innate’s Element requirements but has no cards in hand, no Energy and no ordinary Card Plays left. Can it use that Innate at the proper speed, what Energy or Card Play cost does it ordinarily have, and is it automatically available every turn?
actual_required_facts: The eligible unused Innate may be used at its proper Speed without cards in hand, Energy or Card Plays.
Unless explicitly specified otherwise, it costs no Energy or Card Play.
Innates are automatically available each turn when their requirements are met.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: Without an effect granting a Repeat or another use, may a Spirit pay a Power Card's printed Energy cost twice to use it twice in one turn? If a Slow Power is made Fast, may it be used once in Fast and again in Slow?
actual_required_facts: No second use is granted by paying the printed Energy cost again.
A Power made Fast has its one use in Fast, not one in Fast plus one in Slow.
Another use requires an explicit permission such as Repeat.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: A Spirit plays and pays for a Power Card, then foregoes its entire text because it has no legal target or the Spirit chooses not to use it. With no other effect removing the card, do its printed Elements remain available for Innates, is its Energy refunded, and does the card leave play immediately or during Time Passes?
actual_required_facts: The card's printed Elements remain available while it stays in play despite foregoing all text.
Its Energy is not refunded.
Foregoing its text does not make it immediately leave play.
Normally discard it at Time Passes and lose its Elements then.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: Spirit A uses Powerstorm on Bringer of Dreams and Nightmares. Afterwards Bringer uses Call on Midnight’s Dream in a legal land with Dahan, gains a Fast Major Power, Forgets Call on Midnight’s Dream for the Major gain, and uses its conditional permission to play the new Major immediately. Bringer then uses that new Major normally. Assume sufficient Energy, valid targets, and no other restrictions. May Bringer spend the previously granted Powerstorm Repeat on this new Major even though it was not in play when Powerstorm resolved?
actual_required_facts: Yes: Powerstorm's once-this-turn Repeat permission belongs to the Spirit and is not a snapshot of cards in play at grant time.
The newly played Major is eligible even though it entered play after Powerstorm resolved.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: Bringer uses Call on Midnight’s Dream in a legal target land containing both Dahan and Invaders. May Bringer first draw and inspect the four Major Power Cards from the first option, then decide to take the other option’s 2 Fear instead, or must the ~or~ option be chosen before either option begins resolving?
actual_required_facts: Choose the or branch before resolving either option.
Drawing/inspecting the Major cards already begins the Major-gain option.
It cannot inspect that draw and then switch to the 2 Fear option.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: When using a beginner Spirit’s Power Progression, what must be done during setup with the Minor and Major cards listed on that Progression? Should they stay in the shared shuffled decks to be drawn normally by other gains?
actual_required_facts: During Power Progression setup, set aside all listed Minor and Major Power Cards.
Those reserved cards do not remain in the shared shuffled decks for ordinary draws.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: Entwined Power’s target Spirit draws four cards for its gain and keeps one. For the using Spirit’s subsequent gain, does that Spirit draw a fresh set of four, or select from the three cards the target did not keep? In solo, are the two cards gained through this base effect selected from one initial draw or two?
actual_required_facts: For Entwined's subsequent gain, the using Spirit selects one of the cards the target did not keep from the initial draw; it does not draw a fresh four.
In solo the two cards gained through this base effect come from the same initial draw of four, not two independent draws.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: With Entwined Power’s threshold met, can only the target Spirit gift a card to the using Spirit, or may each gift one to the other? May a gifted card come from cards in play or personal discard instead of hand, and is either gift mandatory?
actual_required_facts: The using Spirit and target Spirit may each gift one Power Card to the other.
Gifts must come from hand; cards in play and personal discard are ineligible.
Each Spirit may independently decline its gift.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: If Powerstorm grants a Spirit a Repeat of a Power Card that it already paid to play, must that Spirit pay the card’s Energy cost again to use that Repeat?
actual_required_facts: Yes; to use that Powerstorm Repeat, pay the repeated Power Card's Energy cost again, in addition to the original play payment.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: A Spirit with no Energy remaining receives Gift of Strength and has already used an eligible cost-1 Power Card. May it use that card's Repeat without paying its cost again, or does Gift require the same repayment as Powerstorm?
actual_required_facts: The eligible Gift of Strength Repeat requires no additional Energy payment and may be used with zero Energy remaining.

families.source_based_comparison: Actual asks include gain4/keep1/reshuffle, Major Forget zones and already-resolved effects, no combining independent Forget payments, deferred Repeat choice, gained-later Major eligibility and explicit Powerstorm versus free Gift payment. No new Repeat-before-first-use rule inferred from an unstated premise.

families.source_family: Targeting, Range, Speed, Elements, thresholds and normal Repeat choices

primary_source_refs.locator: CORE Power attributes, ordered text and thresholds
Complete focused Spirit-targeting internal Range FAQ

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: Explain how Elements apply to multiple thresholds and multiple Powers. May an innate be used twice with twice the Elements, may its levels use different lands, and how does an “Instead” level work?
actual_required_facts: Elements are checked rather than spent and can meet multiple thresholds and Powers.
Extra Elements do not give another ordinary Innate use.
An Innate's levels belong to one Power and use one target.
An Instead level replaces previous levels' effects rather than adding to them.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: A legal target lacks pieces needed for one printed instruction. May the Power still be used? May the player choose individual unwanted instructions to skip, or forego the whole Power and recover its Energy?
actual_required_facts: A legal target remains legal even if an effect instruction is impossible.
Do as much as possible: resolve possible instructions and skip impossible parts.
Do not cherry-pick possible mandatory instructions.
The Spirit may forego the whole Power but receives no Energy refund.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: Does increased Power Range extend Gather/Push distance, may multiple pieces come from/go to different adjacent lands, may pieces go into the Ocean normally, and may “up to” be zero?
actual_required_facts: Range boosts do not change the adjacent-land distance of Gather/Push.
Gather brings pieces from adjacent land(s) into the target.
Push sends pieces from the target to adjacent land(s), allowing different destinations.
Multiple pieces may come from different source lands.
Ordinary movement cannot send them into Ocean/off-board.
Up to permits zero.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: What makes two lands adjacent, including across boards? Are all outside-edge lands Coastal, is Ocean normally a land, and can a land be adjacent to itself or within Range 1 of itself?
actual_required_facts: Adjacent lands share a border or corner, including across boards.
Coastal means adjacent to printed Ocean; other outside cliffs do not count.
Ocean is normally not a land or in play.
A land is not adjacent to itself but is Range 0 of itself and within Range 1.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: Does one Presence each from two Spirits form a Sacred Site? Does four Presence from one Spirit count as two sites, and what does “your land” mean?
actual_required_facts: One disk each from two Spirits does not ordinarily form a Sacred Site.
A Spirit normally needs at least two of its own disks.
Four of its disks in one land still form only one site.
Your land means a land with your Presence.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: A Power’s earlier instruction uncovers an Element needed for a later threshold. Can that later threshold apply? What if Elements are lost instead, and can earlier resolved effects be revised?
actual_required_facts: An Element gained earlier in a Power can satisfy a later threshold.
Losing Elements can prevent a later threshold.
Do not revise already resolved effects retroactively.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: Must a land at Range 0 contain your Presence? Can a numeric Range boost waive a Sacred Site origin, a target-terrain restriction or the text “one of your lands”?
actual_required_facts: An ordinary Range 0 target contains your Presence.
A numeric Range increase does not waive a Sacred Site/origin restriction.
It does not waive terrain or other target contents restrictions, including one of your lands.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: May a legally targeted Power count as used if its instructions accomplish nothing? Does foregoing its text count as targeting it? Can an innate with only its own Speed/Range modification available be used?
actual_required_facts: A legal Power may count as used even if its attempted instructions change nothing.
It needs an instruction with potential to affect game state.
Foregoing its text is not using/targeting it.
Changing only its own Speed/Range does not make an Innate usable.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: Do increased Range and a large number of pieces let a single ordinary Power distribute its effects across multiple target lands? What does Push up to 3 Explorer/Town allow in terms of total pieces?
actual_required_facts: An ordinary Power has one target land regardless of Range or piece count.
Only explicit instructions can affect other lands, such as Push destinations.
Up to 3 Explorer/Town is a combined limit of 3 pieces of either/both types, not 3 each.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: If Gather 3 or Push 3 lacks “up to,” may the player move only one when three legal pieces are available? What if only two are available? Can unrestricted Move leave a piece in its current land?
actual_required_facts: Without up to, move the stated number if possible, so not only one when three are available.
If only two can legally be moved, move both.
Unrestricted Move may leave a piece in the same land and still counts as movement.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: If a Power’s Range was increased and it was made Fast, what happens on Repeat? If Elements enabling a non-Range threshold have been lost, does the Repeat automatically retain that threshold?
actual_required_facts: Range and Speed modifications carry over to Repeat, retaining the boosted Range and Fast Speed.
Other thresholds check current Elements and may no longer apply after Elements are lost.

actual_asked_comparisons.literal_question: A Power was used Fast, then is explicitly made Slow before its ordinary Repeat. Which phase does the Repeat use? What if its text explicitly tells you to Repeat immediately?
